analyst_view.overall: Early view: Hearts (32nd, one point) are in a bad patch: a 7-1 defeat at Celtic, a League Cup semi-final loss to Hibernian and a 3-1 defeat at Thun, where Wouter Vrancken was without ten players and Stephen Kingsley went off injured. Monaco (4th, nine points, one goal conceded) have won all three league-phase games but are only seventh in Ligue 1 and lost 3-1 at Paris FC on 1 November; Ansu Fati is out for about two months, while Folarin Balogun was added to their European squad. Hearts need a result at Tynecastle to stay in the race.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, 2.5 for Monaco. I lean lower: Monaco have conceded once in three European games and won 2-1, 3-0 and 2-0, so their matches have averaged under three goals. Hearts were described by Sky Sports as only sporadically threatening at Thun, so most of the scoring should come from one side.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Hearts leaned heavily on set pieces at Thun (their goal came from a Jordi Altena free-kick headed in by Stuart Findlay), and the home crowd will push them to win corners, but Monaco should have more of the ball. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean a little higher: Hearts at home, needing points and short of players, are likely to press and chase, which tends to bring fouls against a quicker, technical side. No referee is known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots. Hearts' home crowd should push them forward more than at Thun, while Monaco control games without huge shot volumes; I see nothing to move the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Hearts struggled to test the keeper at Thun beyond a long-range effort from Josh McPake and their set pieces, and Monaco's wins have been efficient rather than shot-heavy.
